To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed new methods for the numerical study of codim 2 local bifurcations in dynamical systems, we have applied these new methods to study the dynamics of several known and novel ODEs and we have discovered a number of novel dynamical phenomena, in particular the existence of 3- and 4-toroidal attractors in a novel model from Population Biology.

the codim 2 Neimark-Sackers of limit cycles in 4-dimensional ODEs are more complex than the corresponding codim 2 saddle-node and period-doubling bifurcations; the codim 4 double Neimark Sacker is even more complicated.

the normal form analysis of codim 2 limit cycle bifurcations can be carried out in a systematic manner, and that it is a useful tool to predict the dynamics near these bifurcations, including the existence of stable 3- and 4-torii, and chaos.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic numerical study of codim 2 normal forms for limit cycles with center manifolds of high dimension.
the development of a computational methodology for the numerical analysis of codim 2 normal forms and the numerical computation of Lyapunov characteristic exponents.
the study of codim 2 local bifurcations in ODEs with the center manifold of dimension equal or higher than 3, and with the computation of Lyapunov spectra for the resulting normal forms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the normal form theory is a powerful tool for the analysis of codim 2 limit cycles in ODEs.
our normal form analysis is a powerful tool for a qualitative and quantitative study of complicated bifurcations and chaos in generic autonomous ODES, which is demonstrated in our examples.

the codimension-2 bifurcational behavior of the three models is very similar to the one of the well known Lorenz model, but with the important difference that in the latter the dimension of the center manifolds of the two codim 2 points is 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new approach for numerical bifurcation analysis of codim 2 Hopf bifurcations in higher dimensions.
the numerical periodic normalization technique can be used as a tool for the numerical analysis of complicated bifurcations in higher dimensions.
the periodic normal forms for the codim 2 limit cycle bifurcations with center manifold of dimensions 4 and 5 are obtained in a form suitable for numerical implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
numerical periodic normalization of codim 2 limit cycle bifurcations is a powerful tool in studying the complicated bifurcations which can happen near them.

the periodic normalization technique is a useful tool for the analysis and computation of codim 2 normal forms of limit cycle bifurcations with center manifold dimension higher than three, and can be applied in a wide range of applications.
numerical periodic normal forms are a powerful tool to understand and predict complicated bifurcation phenomena of limit cycles.
